quote.text: You act like mortals in all that you fear, and like immortals in all that you desire
quote.author: Lucius Annaeus Seneca
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood:
    • Recognize that as parents, our fears—worrying about the impermanence of circumstance and the vulnerabilities of our children—are a natural part of our mortal condition; yet, these concerns should balance with the hope and ambition we instill in them.
    • Embrace a dual mindset by teaching your children to be cautious like mortals in the face of danger while nurturing their dreams and aspirations as if they were immortal, encouraging resilience and vision.
  • Leadership:
    • As a leader, understand that fear often stems from our mortal limitations and can paralyze progress; acknowledge these fears, analyze them, and use them as a guide to prepare rather than as a deterrent.
    • Channel the boundless desire typical of those who act like immortals by setting visionary goals and inspiring your team to transcend ordinary limits, always with a grounded understanding of reality.
  • Product Management:
    • In product management, it's important to remain pragmatic—address the finite risks and limitations (our mortal fears) that come with market volatility, competition, and technological challenges.
    • Simultaneously, allow your innovative spirit to soar like that of the immortal, dreaming big and pursuing breakthroughs, but balance ambition with meticulous planning and realistic assessments.
